review.disposition: fixed by reducing the file below the limit outright, not by baseline registration. The session's own Stop hook (a separate, stricter session-level bloat gate than the pre-commit anti-ratchet hook) hard-blocked on ANY session-touched file currently over 300 lines, including this one at its pre-existing 304 — reverting my own additions was not sufficient to clear it. Splitting is out of scope for a SIMPLIFY iterate, and a full bloat-exception ADR (Ousterhout argument, YAGNI check, Chesterton-Fence check) was disproportionate for a pre-existing overage this iterate did not create. Instead, the extraction itself had created genuine new duplication the hook's block surfaced: `test_op_in_progress_says_yes_when_only_the_gitpath_probe_times_out` (exercising `so._op_in_progress`) and `test_reconcile_op_in_progress_gitpath_timeout_also_fails_closed` (exercising `rt._op_in_progress`) now drive the exact same `mtg.op_in_progress` through its two re-export aliases, with a byte-identical closure duplicated between them. Merged into one `@pytest.mark.parametrize`d test over both aliases; also dropped the redundant `assert rt._op_in_progress is mtg.op_in_progress` (and the earlier `so` one), since `test_triage_write_path_contracts.py`'s `_PRIVATE_ALIASES` table already asserts both object identities (`assert old is new`, line 123) in a file with headroom. File is now 297 lines — under the limit, coverage preserved (both aliases still separately exercised via parametrize IDs), and the fix is itself a legitimate simplification the extraction motivated, not an unrelated cleanup.
